title: Engineering Intern
description: About Atira Atira builds the commercial brain for industrials. Our agents 10x the sales engineers of today by offering the complete toolbox of tasks needed in complex environments. They handle everything from extracting and classifying requirements from incoming RFQs, orchestrating communication and information retrieval across multiple stakeholders and systems, while generating outcomes like documentation, production system inputs, or configuration recommendations. CRM. Atira. ERP. We are one of the fastest growing teams in Munich and are looking for you to join us! Why engineers are the foundation of everything Atira ships As an Engineering Intern at Atira, you will work on frontier AI technology, such as (recursive) agent harnesses, runtimes, evals, inference and self-verification in complex engineering domains. You build the frameworks, primitives and scaffolding that let agents reliably handle complex industrial processes end to end, from the first inbound RFQ to the write-back into ERP. Misreading or wrongly interpreting a spec can cost a manufacturer six figures, so the challenges are real and the margin for error is thin. Where you trained matters less than what you've built and how clearly you can describe what broke. Atira is at a stage where you must own problems end to end, because what you ship today is what our customers use tomorrow. What you will do Work on the agent runtime and harnesses. You improve the core components that let Atira's agents reason in complex engineering environments across the entire sales-engineering lifecycle, orchestrate themselves recursively at scale through dynamic programs, and handle arbitrarily large amounts of data. This includes the runtime/sandboxing, the harness, and the outer orchestration layer that ties it together Build out our AI moat. You are in charge of improving quality & evals, improving the ontology layer that unlocks compounding process knowledge and fusing deterministic guardrails with agentic agency to make our agents actionable at enterprise level complexity Unlock industrial scale. Industrials live in multi-modal, data-heavy environments: 1000-page inbounds, pricing lists, CAD files, ERP tables, legacy applications. You scale the AI systems behind them to millions of concurrent LLM requests in isolated sandboxes, with no silent failures, cost blowouts or latency explosions. Advance our internal tooling. FDEs, platform engineers and the GTM team depend on tooling you build to improve Atira's internal context layer, ambient agents, insight and observability engines Work with FDEs when customer problems hit the platform. When an FDE hits a problem they should be able to pull you in. At a team of 20, the boundary between AI, platform and customer is thin, and you'll cross it regularly What we are looking for Ownership, depth, and the instinct to take problems personally, go deep until you understand the system, and own the outcome including the parts that broke. Your profile Agent fluency sits on top of real engineering fundamentals. Solid skills in Python, TypeScript, or a comparable language. We value someone that can still code without AI. Ideally paired with hands-on experience with agents, evals, harnesses, runtimes, sandboxing and tools You've gone further than most with AI-assisted development. Whether it's Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or your own setup, you've invested seriously in building the skills, context, and workflows to get maximum leverage from coding agents. This isn't a nice-to-have. We think engineers who have mastered this are fundamentally more productive, and we hire accordingly You reason clearly about technical tradeoffs. You don’t need to have run systems at scale yet, but you can think through how a design would hold up at thousands of requests per second and explain the pros and cons of different approaches. Every design has tradeoffs: no free lunch You’ve demonstrated ownership and initiative. A side project you took further than anyone asked, a serious open-source contribution, a research project or a startup. We want evidence that you build without being told to and can explain what broke and why You have a strong technical foundation. Enrolled or recently graduated in Computer Science, Information Systems, AI, or a related technical field from a strong technical university (cracked dropouts can qualify too though) Full working proficiency in English. German is not required You're ready for a real internship, not a side gig. You can commit to at least three months full-time, on-site in Munich What you'll get Real ownership: you'll be one of the early team members and shape both product and architecture as well as work closely with customers Strong peers and mentorship: work with and learn from engineers who have shipped AI systems in industrial environments at scale, with the opportunity for mentorship along the way Impactful work: your code is deployed all across Europe’s and US industrial backbone, affecting how complex products and services are sold and configured worldwide Competitive salary and additional benefits Most importantly: Collaborate & thrive in a high-performing but caring culture. We will own the industrial sales function but will do so with modesty and integrity What success looks like at the end of the internship You've shipped meaningful improvements to the agent runtime, our AI pipelines and related systems that are running in production across multiple customer deployments You own one well-defined piece of our AI stack end to end (an eval suite, an internal tool, part of the context layer or the SDK), and the team trusts your judgment on how it should evolve When something breaks in the part you own, you can trace it end to end, from agent behaviour back to the agent infrastructure layer, and fix it You’ve made an improvement to our internal AI tooling that the team now uses day to day The design decisions in your piece have held up under real load, and you can explain the tradeoffs you made and what you’d do differently If these metrics are met, we'd take you full-time without thinking twice Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

description: Company Description Experian is a global data and technology company, powering opportunities for people and businesses around the world. We operate across a range of markets, from financial services to healthcare, automotive, agribusiness, insurance, and many more. Job Description The Software Engineer (.NET/Azure) is a hands-on, mid-level contributor responsible for designing, building, and modernizing high-volume, high-transaction applications across the Experian Employer Services (EES) organization. You will write production code, participate in code reviews, evaluate SAST findings, and work closely with product, quality engineering, security, and operations partners to deliver secure, reliable software to our clients and partners. AI and automation are the main focus of our team. EES is adopting an AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AI DLC) and spec-driven agentic development, in which teams define intent, constraints, acceptance criteria, and validation before AI agents build approved work. As an engineer in this model you will work from versioned specifications, direct AI coding agents to implement approved work, and oversee the review, testing, and security validation of what they produce. You will have already worked this way hands-on; this is a requirement of the role, not a learning goal. Humans remain accountable for technical decisions, data protection, and production outcomes. At Experian, we believe great work happens when people come together. We're focused on attracting talent in and around our designated hub locations who are open to collaborating with colleagues in person. Aligning employees to these talent markets helps foster collaboration, strengthen team connections, and support long-term career growth within Experian. This hybrid role reports to the Engineering Manager, Application Engineering, and reside in or near one of our collaboration hubs: Costa Mesa, CA; San Jose, CA; Allen, TX; Austin, TX; Franklin, TN; New York, NY; Schaumberg, IL; Washington, D.C.; Atlanta, GA; Boston, MA; Seattle, WA Responsibilities: Analyze new feature requirements with attention to design, software development best practices, testing strategy, database design, security, and cloud architecture, and turn them into clear, versioned specifications with explicit acceptance criteria that engineers and AI agents can verify. Use AI coding assistants and agents (for example GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, or similar) to implement approved work, and own the review, testing, and security validation of AI-generated code before it is merged. Decide when a change needs additional human review based on its risk. Build new and modernize existing .NET applications, APIs, and partner integrations, including responsive, accessible web UIs that work across devices.
